set.typical_award_size: Davis is a CDBG entitlement city and a HOME participating jurisdiction. HUD formula allocations: FY 2025 CDBG $730,016 and HOME $323,760 (about $1.05 million combined); FY 2026 CDBG $700,471 and HOME $309,807 (about $1.01 million). Council adopted the 2025-2029 Consolidated Plan and the Program Year One (2025) Annual Action Plan on April 15, 2025 (Resolution 25-061). HOME has historically funded first-time homebuyer loans and rental project gap loans; CDBG funds public services, facilities and homelessness programs. PLHA: HCD's 2024-2028 Formula Allocation NOFA (July 16, 2026) lists Davis at $212,632 for CY 2024 and $227,760 for CY 2025, with an estimated $1,328,950 over five years; staff said in February 2025 that PLHA would go to homeownership opportunities.
set.cycle_notes: CDBG and HOME follow an annual Action Plan adopted each spring after a public hearing. PLHA formula funds flow through the City's five-year plan; under HCD's 2024-2028 NOFA the City must apply for the CY 2024 allocation by the end of February 2028 and the CY 2025 allocation by the end of February 2029.
set.next_deadline: No open round as of November 10, 2026. The Program Year 2027 Action Plan process is expected winter to spring 2027 with a public hearing typically in April; confirm amounts and the HOME set-aside with Grants Management, (530) 757-5602.
set.audit_note: NC audit Nov 10, 2026: April 15, 2025 minutes confirm Resolution 25-061; HUD FY 2025 and FY 2026 CPD formula allocation spreadsheets give Davis CDBG and HOME amounts (replacing the press figure); HCD 2024-2028 PLHA NOFA Appendix A gives the Davis CY 2024, CY 2025 and five-year PLHA figures. Next cycle relabeled Program Year 2027.

set.typical_award_size: HCD's PLHA formula award list shows West Sacramento awarded $763,253 on May 22, 2025 for its 2021, 2022 and 2023 formula allocations ($404,832, $202,903 and $155,518, with $38,163 allowable admin) for eligible activities 1 and 7. HCD's 2024-2028 Formula Allocation NOFA (July 16, 2026) lists West Sacramento at $166,132 for CY 2024 and $177,952 for CY 2025, with an estimated $1,038,325 over five years.

set.typical_award_size: West Sacramento became a CDBG entitlement city in FY 2016/17. HUD formula allocations: FY 2025 CDBG $546,333 and FY 2026 CDBG $517,683, with no HOME allocation (the City is not a HOME participating jurisdiction). A draft 2026-2030 Consolidated Plan and FY 2026-27 Annual Action Plan were reported out for comment in spring 2026 (City notice not opened). Housing uses have been infrastructure for affordable projects ($1,191,428 of CDBG program income for West Gateway Place Phase 1), fair housing services, homeless coordinator staffing, a supportive housing project allocation ($415,862 of CDBG entitlement and program income), first-time homebuyer help and owner rehabilitation. The City holds HOME program income from earlier state HOME awards (a developer fact sheet reports $2,000,000 into West Gateway Place II). State LHTF ($1,000,000) and state CDBG ($551,720) applications were not awarded.
set.next_deadline: No open round as of November 10, 2026. The FY 2027-28 Action Plan comment period is expected about March to April 2027; subrecipient applications typically open in winter. Confirm with the Housing Division.

set.typical_award_size: Kaiser reports $400 million committed toward housing stability and affordability with a goal of 30,000 housing units created or preserved by 2030; the Thriving Communities Fund provides capital and long-term loans to acquire, develop and maintain multiunit properties. The RxHome Fund, launched in 2018 with Enterprise Community Loan Fund, is a $100 million loan fund ($50 million each from Kaiser and ECLF) of low-cost, long-term debt for affordable multifamily rental housing in Kaiser service areas including California; by December 2023 it had leveraged $252 million more ECLF capital and supported 7,167 units. Kaiser is also the anchor investor in Enterprise's Housing for Health Fund, a preservation equity fund. Loan terms and current availability are not posted.
set.next_deadline: No published application round as of November 10, 2026; contact Enterprise Community Loan Fund (RxHome) or Enterprise's Northern California office (Housing for Health Fund).
set.layering_notes: Reclassified from other to loan: Kaiser's housing page says the Thriving Communities Fund provides capital and long-term loans to acquire, develop and maintain multiunit properties; RxHome is a $100 million debt fund with Enterprise Community Loan Fund (Enterprise blog, December 18, 2023). The Housing for Health Fund is a separate preservation equity vehicle; earlier passes reported it at $85 million with Enterprise and JPMorgan Chase in the Bay Area and Sacramento, but those figures were not confirmed on pages opened in the Nov 10, 2026 audit. Kaiser's Northern California service area covers the Bay Area, Sacramento, Stockton, Fresno and Santa Cruz.
set.audit_note: NC audit Nov 10, 2026: Kaiser housing security page confirms $400 million, 30,000 units by 2030 and Thriving Communities Fund long-term loans; Enterprise blog (December 18, 2023) confirms RxHome terms and 7,167 units. Housing for Health Fund dollar figures moved to layering_notes as unconfirmed.

reason: Kaiser and Enterprise pages confirm the commitment, Thriving Communities Fund loans and RxHome terms; unconfirmed Housing for Health Fund figures were moved out of the award size.
